Sensitive philanthropic terms such as 'fondation' without specific government recognition for charitable entities

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (routine verification during incorporation and annual filings; unannounced inspections rare for standard charitable entities)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation, governance, and dissolution); Law No. 87-571 of 23 July 1987 on the development of sponsorship (for charitable endowment activities); Decree No. 2020-109 of 10 February 2020 on the registration of companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) executed in writing, accompanied by the M0 form (déclaration de création d'entreprise) and supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL; however, capital must be fully subscribed and at least 50% of cash contributions paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within 5 years. For charitable endowment activities, a dedicated endowment fund (fonds de dotation) may be required, subject to prefecture approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby adopt the Articles of Association of the SARL, and that the share capital of EUR 10,000 is subscribed and paid as per the terms. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at 12 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France. RESOLVED, that Mr. Jean Dupont is appointed as Manager (Gérant) with full powers to represent the company, and Ms. Marie Curie is appointed as Deputy Manager. RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to complete all filings, registrations, and licensing procedures necessary for the company's charitable endowment activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if real estate contribution) or any legal counsel; final filing to Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, including company name, registered office, share capital, share distribution, management structure, and charitable purpose. Ensure compliance with Article L.223-1 of the Commercial Code. If contributions include real estate, notarize the deed. All shareholders must sign the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of shareholders and managers
Bank certificate of capital deposit (if cash contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Statuts, amend the document to address legal deficiencies and resubmit within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in a Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized legal gazette (e.g., Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice containing the company name, legal form (SARL), capital, registered office, object, and manager details. Obtain a copy of the publication certificate (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is incomplete, republish with corrected information and obtain a new attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed M0 form, signed Statuts, legal notice attestation, capital deposit certificate, and identity documents. Pay the filing fee (approx. EUR 50). The registry will issue a receipt and process the application.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the registry's observations within 30 days, providing additional documentation or clarifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Company Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (same registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful registration, the registry issues an extract K-bis (official certificate of registration) containing the SIREN number, legal form, and registered office. This document serves as proof of legal existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, contact the registry directly; any errors in the extract must be corrected by filing a rectification request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Tax and Social Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and URSSAF (social security)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits registration data to tax and social authorities. However, the company must file a specific declaration for charitable status (if applicable) with the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) to obtain tax-exempt status for philanthropic activities. Also register with URSSAF for employer obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social registration is delayed, contact the respective authority with the K-bis and request expedited processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Préfecture de Police (or local prefecture) and the Ministry of the Interior (for endowment funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SARL operates as a private charitable foundation (fonds de dotation), file a declaration with the prefecture to obtain recognition of public utility or a simple declaration of existence. This may require a separate dossier including the company's charter, financial plan, and governance rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the prefecture rejects the application, revise the dossier to address concerns and resubmit within 30 days. Legal counsel may be engaged to appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture de Police de Paris (or local prefecture) for operating permits; Direction Régionale des Entreprises, de la Concurrence, de la Consommation, du Travail et de l'Emploi (DIRECCTE) for workplace compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exercice d'une activité de gestion de fonds de dotation (Authorization to operate an endowment fund management activity) or Récépissé de déclaration d'activité (Receipt of activity declaration) for charitable operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (via Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement - DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no industrial activity; office-based endowment management only)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation. If any minor office waste, comply with general waste management regulations (Code de l'environnement, Articles R.541-1 et seq.).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire brigade (SDIS) for the registered office; structural load inspection if the premises are not standard office space; workplace health and safety clearance from DIRECCTE confirming compliance with the Labor Code (Code du travail) regarding ergonomics, emergency exits, and first aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – impots.gouv.fr; centralized business formalities portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SARL must register via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), selecting the 'société' filing and uploading the articles of association and identity documents. DGFiP automatically issues SIREN/SIRET registration and allocates the French intra-community VAT number. A non-resident entity without a French establishment that makes taxable supplies must file a direct VAT application through the dedicated DGFiP non-resident procedure; a provisional tax identification number (NIF) is issued pending VAT activation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime; tax classification is statutory. A SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (IS, CGI Art. 206). It may elect for a five-year period, under CGI Art. 239 bis, to be taxed as a transparent partnership (IR). A charitable endowment SARL may also qualify for non-profit exemption under CGI Art. 206(1) if management is disinterested and the activity is non-commercial. VAT grouping is available under CGI Art. 256 C ter; ATAD and DAC6 hybrid mismatch rules apply to elective financing arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA) under Code Général des Impôts, Arts. 256-289.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services under the domestic franchise-in-base exemption (CGI Art. 293 B); non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold and must register for French VAT before making taxable supplies in France, subject to reverse charge or OSS where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: From 1 September 2026, all French-established VAT-taxable persons must receive electronic invoices via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified De-materialisation Partner Platform (PDP); issuance obligations phase in from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small enterprises. Structured e-invoice formats (Factur-X/UBL) must be transmitted by API to DGFiP for mandatory e-reporting; no real-time fiscal stamping applies, but the digital transmission pipeline and archiving are legally mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% (exemption with credit) applies to dispatches or transports of goods to destinations outside the EU (CGI Art. 262-I-1) and to certain services directly related to exported goods (CGI Art. 262-I-2) or consumed outside the EU under CGI Art. 259. The supplier must be VAT-registered, hold ownership or export mandate, prove the goods left France/EU under an accepted customs export procedure, and retain complete documentary evidence before claiming zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation via DELTA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Proof of payment / Inward Remittance Certificate (avis de crédit or attestation de domiciliation bancaire)
Export sales contract or purchase order
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, if export evidence is incomplete or the export did not in fact occur, VAT at 20% is clawed back plus intérêt de retard (0.20% per month) and statutory penalties under CGI Art. 1729: 40% for deliberate understatement and 80% for organized fraud. Criminal tax fraud under CGI Art. 1741 may result in imprisonment for up to five years and fines up to EUR 500,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), exercising monetary and balance-of-payments statistics authority within the Eurosystem; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) supervises credit institutions and payment institutions, and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) administers sanctions and restrictive measures, all under the Code Monétaire et Financier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; France applies the EU free movement of capital and payments regime (TFEU Articles 63-66). Both current and capital account operations are liberalised, with no exchange-control licensing, no surrender obligation and no ceiling on foreign-currency holding for the SARL. Profit or endowment remittances to foreign beneficiaries are unrestricted in FX terms but remain subject to EU/UN sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering due diligence, and, where a beneficiary is a dividend-paying structure, to the French withholding-tax framework on outbound distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion ratio applies to export or service receipts in France; proceeds may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency. The only binding obligation is statistical reporting: the resident entity must report all cross-border transactions to Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes (monthly ECL/RUBRIQUE declarations where thresholds are exceeded), and cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more across the EU border must be declared to French Customs (DGDDI) under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672. Verification basis: 0% mandatory conversion; 100% free retainability.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: LCL – Le Crédit Lyonnais (Crédit Agricole Group)
Crédit Mutuel & CIC (Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Endowment Custody Account
Endowment Custody and FX Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for French-licensed EMIs: High for operational accounts (Qonto, Kaiko, Vialink Panenka), but Medium overall because an endowment manager requires multi-currency treasury, segregated custody, and grant-disbursement rails beyond the EMI licence perimeter. EU-passported EMIs (German, Irish, Dutch digital banks) are Lawful Under the ACPR passporting regime and may hold the operational account on behalf of a French SARL. Non-EU and offshore digital EMIs (post-Brexit UK, US, Singapore, Baltic non-bank fintechs without French/EU passport) are rated Low: they cannot lawfully provide payment services to a French resident without ACPR authorisation or a full EU branch, and French banks will not clear or accept them as intermediary references.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical interview of at least one SARL gérant (managing director) and, where applicable, the final beneficial owner is the default ACPR expectation: the bank must verify identity, capacity, and source of funds in person or by an equivalent certified notarial/juristic verification. Remote onboarding is legally permitted under EBA/GL/2022/06 (remote customer due diligence), but for a private charitable foundation with endowment classification, the compliance committee of tier-1 banks almost always requires either a physical meeting at a French branch, or an assisted video-verification accompanied by (i) the original or up-to-date statuts of the SARL, (ii) the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract, (iii) the prefectural declaration or decree recognising the charitable purpose, and (iv) a power of attorney (pouvoir) with apostille for any foreign director who cannot appear.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained large donations or lump-sum capital injections inconsistent with the declared endowment purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete source-of-funds file: notarised donation deed (acte de donation), donor identity and passport, upstream bank statements covering 12 months, the SARL's minute book entry approving the capital/endowment increase, audited or accountant-certified financial statements, and a written philanthropic rationale mapping each inflow to ISIC 6430 / NAICS 813211 grant-making activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restrictive-measure screening hits on grant beneficiaries or donor counterparties (EU consolidated list, UN lists, US OFAC SDN, French CISLE list)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adverse-media-cleared counterparty file: full name, date of birth and tax residency of each beneficiary, a negative screening certificate issued by an independent screening tool, COREP/AML transaction justification, a signed sanctions-compliance warranty clause from the beneficiary, and a documented grant-approval memorandum evidencing legitimate humanitarian or scientific end-use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incorrect or incomplete CRS/FATCA and French tax residency self-certification, particularly with a foreign founder or foreign grant recipients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CERFA 3916-sd / OECD CRS self-certification forms for each account, the legal entity classification statement (FATCA NFFE or FFI), certificate of tax domicile for non-resident chairman/donors, the SARL's French SIRET/RNA registration documentation, and, where the foundation solicits foreign funds, the French authorisation for public collection (appel public à la générosité) granted by the prefecture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: nominee shareholder arrangements or a refusal to disclose the ultimate donor chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date RBE filing receipt, organisational chart and ownership cascade, statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) certification of the capital structure, signed declarations of trust or nominee prohibition, and a legal opinion confirming that the SARL holding company for the private charitable endowment is not controlled, directly or indirectly, by a politically exposed person or a shell company in a high-risk jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound endowment and capital-contribution wires are routed via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA equivalent for EEA donors) to the SARL's French IBAN with the ISO 20022 business purpose code DIPP (Direct Investment) or 'CHAR/DON' where the donated funds are not consideration; the bank file must evidence the notarised capital increase, the source of funds, and the RBE/UBO declarations. Cross-border amounts equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 carried in cash require the DGDDI cash declaration; bank-transferred sums are covered by the five-day validation of the beneficiary bank plus the automatic Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting. For non-EEA donor jurisdictions, the intermediary must be an EU correspondent bank with clean MT 202 cover statements, and the receiving bank requires an LTV (lettre de venue) or pro-forma funding instruction to avoid quarantine.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant disbursements within the euro area are executed through SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant clearing (TARGET2/TIPS), while non-EEA grant distributions and procurement settlements use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers via the SARL's French correspondent bank, with UETR for end-to-end traceability. Commercial letter-of-credit settlements (UCP 600) are available for large scientific-equipment or humanitarian procurement, opened by the French relationship bank and cleared through banks in Germany, Switzerland, the UK or the United States. All outbound disbursements must carry the EU purpose code for grants (e.g., 'GRANT', 'TRUST', or 'CHAR'), be pre-validated against the EU/UN consolidated sanctions lists, and be reported for Banque de France statistical purposes where aggregate monthly customer transfers exceed the reporting threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable foreign exchange forwards executed under an ISDA or FBF master agreement with an ACPR-authorised EU credit institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-convertible currencies where the underlying philanthropic exposure requires hedge protection
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term endowment liabilities denominated in USD, GBP or CHF
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term treasury liquidity management between EUR and other freely convertible currencies
OTC European-style FX options (calls/puts) on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP for downside protection, subject to the SARL's MiFID-classified professional status and AMF suitability requirements

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of financial statements — minutes (procès-verbal) recorded in the minuted register
stage_5.receiving_authority: None (internal statutory register; the approved minutes underpin the subsequent greffe filing)
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December FYE), extendable by court order
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Late or absent AGM: manager is liable for the filing irregularity; shareholders/any interested party may ask the court to order a meeting; criminal fine up to €6,000 for the manager (art. L.244-1 et seq.).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate; reduced 15% rate applies to first €38,120 of taxable profit for companies with qualified turnover below €10 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for SARL endowment entities. Deductions include research tax credit (crédit d'impôt recherche, rate up to 30%), family and charitable donation credits, and territorial solidarity exemption for certain not-for-profit ancillary activities. Income from conventional endowment management remains CIT-chargable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 and supplementary forms (2033 series) filed electronically through impots.gouv.fr (EDI-TDFC or EFI) for all companies subject to CIT, including non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by the second working day following 1 May in the next year. For non-calendar fiscal years, the return must be filed within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal form, SIREN, RCS registration, registered office address, and principal activity (NAF code).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report the French branch identity and French SIREN number; only the permanent establishment activity is described.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates tax regime: régime réel normal or régime réel simplifié; includes option for tax consolidation under Article 223 A CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE is required to file under the real normal regime; cannot opt for simplified regime unless expressly qualified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or deficit after reinstatement of non-deductible items, depreciation, and asset disposals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only profits attributable to the French permanent establishment, determined under the separate entity / authorized OECD approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reliefs (research integrity, international credit, charitable donation credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE can only claim credits directly attributable to French-source income; attach Form 2069 and supporting schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% of net tax due if filed within 30 days after deadline, increased to 40% if no filing after formal notice; plus late payment interest of 0.2% per month and, in aggravated cases, 80% penalty for abus de droit or insincere declarations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties_note: Non-filing penalties apply to formal 2065 schedules as well as unpaid prepayments (split monthly or quarterly).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% flat levy (prélèvement forfaitaire unique) plus social levies for non-resident individual shareholders, subject to treaty overriding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty withholding rate, the beneficial owner must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (Form 5000 issued by the foreign tax authority) to the French paying company before the dividend payment date. The certified form must include the identification of the French company, the shareholder, and the holding period. Paying entity is legally required to apply the reduced rate only after receipt and verification of the certificate. The certificate must be preserved for at least 6 years and produced to French tax authorities upon request.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding rate 33.33% (or 0% for EU-qualifying payments under the Interest & Royalties Directive if beneficial ownership and substance requirements are met). Interest: domestic withholding rate 25% on fixed-return debt receivables payable by a French debtor; treaty rates commonly 0% for arm's-length financings, but a valid TRC is mandatory for each interest payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million group turnover AND (i) EUR 8 million intra-group transactions with the French entity, or (ii) French entity itself exceeding EUR 400 million turnover. Thresholds applied per Article L13 AA of the French Tax Code.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a zero-tier Economic Substance Regulation of the kind seen in offshore financial centres. Instead, the l'abus de droit fiscal (abuse of law) doctrine, beneficial ownership criteria, and the anti-shell company framework under EU ATAD (notably DAC6) apply. A charitable endowment SARL must demonstrate actual grant-making activity, board control, and asset management presence; fiscal substance is proven by payroll, real platform, and decision-making files.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing false annual CIT returns, understating endowment income, or creating artificial expenditures to erase taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty of up to 80% of tax deficiencies plus late interest at 0.2% monthly. Criminal fine of EUR 450,000 (increased to EUR 750,000 in aggravated cases) and imprisonment of 5 to 7 years. Repeated offenders are barred from public contracts and subsidies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is available where concealment of assets or criminal intent is proven. Directors face joint civil liability for unpaid taxes and penalties, travel bans against leaving France, and possible citizenship sanctions in treaty states.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abusive Arrangement (abus de droit documentaire)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a non-resident entity or a French SARL with negligible substance purely to divert profits or access a treaty network without genuine business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article L64 CGI, the tax administration may disregard the arrangement and reassess taxes under the real substance of the activity. Sanction includes 80% fine for abuse of law, 10% restriction on interest deductibility, and denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the de facto manager may be held personally liable for the resulting tax deficiencies and 80% penalty; additionally, travel bans and inability to leave the European Economic Area while proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Facilitating fund distributions to sanctioned persons or using the charitable foundation network as a conduit for illicit cash flows, even if the SARL itself is non-banking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, penalties of up to EUR 1 million for institutions and EUR 2 million for repeated or aggravated violations, plus a prohibition on banking activity. Directors may be subject to a fine of EUR 375,000 and 5 years of imprisonment for money laundering offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who knowingly executes an unlawful transfer is jointly and severally liable for the proceeds and for restitution orders issued by the penal court. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure + Charge Fixation Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and file Local File / Master File when thresholds are exceeded, or invoicing intra-group management fees at non-arm's-length rates on the endowment portfolio.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 10,000 for each missing statutory annex, plus a penalty equal to 5% of the reassessment resulting from non-production of TP documents, with a maximum of EUR 100,000 per taxpayer per assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the French entity is assessed and becomes unable to pay, directors may be liable on a de facto management basis. Director travel bans, bank account restrictions, and bans on managing a business for up to 10 years apply when the transfer pricing manipulation is detected as a deliberate misallocation.
